text:
maria (AE): Heads-up — Nimbus Payments wants to migrate from a competitor API to Redwood. They're asking for a 2-week POC to validate prompt parity, response shape, and a short pricing/security brief. They've attached their security questionnaire link: https://files.nimbus/sec-q-2026.pdf. Can we coordinate?

customer-sre (Nimbus): timeline is firm — want POC started next Monday. Main risks: prompt parity for transaction descriptions and function-calling webhooks.

liam (SE): OK. Recommended approach: build a tiny compat shim that accepts their current OpenAPI-style requests and translates to Redwood calls. Key differences to watch for: tokenization + stop behavior, default temperature/top_p, streaming chunking, and function-calling payload shape. We'll run a 10-prompt parity suite (short/long/edge-case prompts) and diff outputs client-side (levenshtein + semantic similarity). If divergence > 12% on business-critical prompts we iterate.

liam (SE): Quick curl example to demo translation (very rough):

```bash
# their OpenAI-like call -> map to Redwood generate endpoint
curl -X POST https://redwood/api/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"model":"x-small-ggml", "input": "translate: Payment of $120 to Acme" , "max_tokens": 60, "temperature": 0.2}'
```

liam (SE): For function-calling, we usually adapt their `name/params` pairs into Redwood's structured output. That adapter is ~1-2 engineer-days for a simple POC.

zoe (Product): Pricing notes for the POC: hosted usage — we can grant a complimentary POC allocation up to 2M tokens and a 50% discount on additional usage during the trial. For production migration we should discuss Redwood Dedicated if they need predictable throughput / egress isolation; I'll put together a back-of-envelope committed capacity quote based on their expected qps.

sam (Security): We need answers for: data residency, retention windows, KMS/HSM integration, and SOC2 + ISO attestations. Maria — please push their questionnaire to me. We can provide a pre-filled SOC2 + KMS section within 48 hours and a VPC/private deployment timeline if needed. Also ask Nimbus if they require IP allowlisting or signed webhooks.

ethan (Eng runtime): A couple of runtime caveats: 1) our cache/kv semantics differ — repeated prefixes may hit cache and change latency profile vs their current provider; 2) function-calling may require a small shim to preserve the exact JSON shape (we've done this before); 3) quantized model variants can affect tokenization edge-cases — include raw byte-level checks in the parity suite. For canary: start 5% traffic to compat shim -> collect metrics (latency, token delta, semantic drift) -> expand. Rollback if critical transforms fail.

liam (SE): Test plan checklist:
- 10 canonical prompts from Nimbus (we need them uploaded)
- 50 random production prompts (they can scrub PII)
- Function-calling roundtrip tests (webhook latency + schema matches)
- Streaming vs non-streaming parity checks
- Latency and cost delta report

maria (AE): Nimbus said they'll upload canonical prompts by EOD today. I'm scheduling kickoff for Monday 10am PT. @liam can you own the POC infra? @zoe will you send the POC pricing note to Nimbus? @sam will you fill the sec questionnaire?

liam (SE): I can own infra. I'll provision a small compat container and a test harness, and push a `poc/nimbus` branch. Expect an env URL by Monday morning.

zoe (Product): Will DM Nimbus the POC pricing and the Dedicated/Reserved spec.

sam (Security): I'll start the questionnaire now and loop in compliance for any non-standard asks.

customer-sre (Nimbus): Thanks — we'll upload prompts and sample webhooks before EOD. Also can you confirm SLA targets for Dedicated? Need 99.95% and max p95 latency 120ms.

ethan (Eng runtime): Noted SLA asks — Dedicated can be configured for that target depending on model and instance sizing. I'll list model/hardware combos that realistically meet 120ms p95.

deploy-bot: POC environment `poc-nimbus-v1` created by liam — URL: https://poc.redwood/internal/poc-nimbus-v1 (tokenized access).

maria (AE): Great, thanks everyone. I'll track actions and update the customer. Any blockers call them out now.

liam (SE): Minor blocker: if Nimbus relies on exact byte-for-byte function output ordering we may need an extra canonicalizer. Otherwise should be straightforward.

sam (Security): If they require air-gapped/hard-residency we'll need to scope Private deployment (timeline 6-8 weeks).

maria (AE): Understood. We'll surface that if it's requested. Meeting invite sent.
